identification.summary: Pink Sandstorm (Agrius) is an Iranian threat actor that has run destructive wiper and fake-ransomware operations, mainly against Israeli organizations [S3][S4]. SentinelLabs first described the group in May 2021 as starting with espionage and moving to wipers disguised as ransomware against Israeli targets [S4][S5]. Microsoft describes Pink Sandstorm as MOIS-linked. Microsoft also reports that the group conducted a hack-and-leak against an Israeli hospital in late November 2023 and has collaborated with Hezbollah cyber units since the October 2023 war began [S1]. Later operations added data theft before wiping, as in Unit 42's 2023 reporting on Israeli higher-education and technology victims [S8][S9].
identification.firstObserved: 2020. MITRE says the group has been active since 2020 [S3], and SentinelOne reported it operating in Israel from the beginning of 2020 [S5].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Pink Sandstorm (formerly AMERICIUM). Microsoft maps SPECTRAL KITTEN, Agrius, Deadwood, BlackShadow, SharpBoys, FireAnt and Justice Blade to it [S2]. MITRE tracks the group as Agrius (G1030) and lists Pink Sandstorm, AMERICIUM, Agonizing Serpens and BlackShadow as associated names [S3]. Palo Alto Unit 42 tracks it as Agonizing Serpens and equates it with Agrius, BlackShadow, Pink Sandstorm and DEV-0022 [S8]. 'Deadwood' is also the name of a wiper (DEADWOOD/Detbosit) that SentinelLabs linked to the group's operations [S4]. Moneybird is a ransomware strain, not a group name [S7]. Microsoft names Pink Sandstorm as 'a.k.a. Agrius' in its February 2024 report [S1].

attribution.sponsor: Iran, with links to the Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS). Microsoft calls Pink Sandstorm an 'MOIS-linked group' [S1]. MITRE notes that public reporting links Agrius to MOIS [S3]. Israeli authorities reportedly attributed the late-2023 Ziv hospital attack to Iran's Ministry of Intelligence, working with Hezbollah [S10].
attribution.confidence: In 2021 SentinelOne assessed with medium confidence that Agrius is of Iranian origin and engaged in both espionage and disruptive activity [S4][S5]. ESET calls the group 'Iran-aligned' [S6]. Unit 42 says it is believed to be sponsored by the Iranian government [S8][S9]. Microsoft's MOIS link is a vendor assessment [S1]. The only government attribution found is Israel's, as press reporting describes it [S10]; no US government attribution was found in the sources gathered here.
attribution.basis: Vendor incident response and malware analysis: SentinelLabs on Apostle, DEADWOOD and IPsec Helper [S4]; ESET on Fantasy and Sandals [S6]; Check Point on Moneybird, as BleepingComputer reports it [S7]; Unit 42 on MultiLayer, PartialWasher and BFG Agonizer [S8]. Microsoft telemetry [S1]. Israeli National Cyber Directorate statements, as press reporting describes them [S10].

objectives: Disruption and destruction of Israeli organizations' systems, disguised as financially motivated ransomware [S4][S7]. SentinelLabs judged that the ransom demands were cover for disruption rather than a profit motive [S4]. Since 2023 the group has also stolen and leaked data (personal data and intellectual property) before wiping, which supports Iranian influence and retaliation goals [S1][S8]. Microsoft framed the November 2023 hospital hack-and-leak as apparent retaliation for Israel's siege of al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza [S1]. SentinelOne also assessed an espionage component [S5].

sectors: Diamond industry and a software supply chain serving it [S6]
Insurance and financial services (Shirbit, per reporting) [S5][S7]
HR consulting and IT support services [S6]
targeting.notes: Israel is the consistent focus across vendors [S4][S6][S8]. ESET's 2022 victims outside Israel (South Africa, Hong Kong) were reached through a supply chain serving the diamond trade, not targeted as countries in their own right [S6]. Shirbit (2020) and Bar-Ilan University (2021) are attributed to Agrius in press coverage of Check Point's work [S7]. The Shirbit attribution in SentinelOne-era reporting comes from unnamed industry sources [S5].

capabilities.summary: Initial access comes through exploitation of known vulnerabilities in public-facing web servers, followed by ASPXSpy-variant web shells [S7][S8]. In the Moneybird case those web shells were hidden in 'Certificate' text files [S7]. The group's custom .NET tooling includes the IPsec Helper backdoor and the Apostle wiper, which it later turned into working ransomware. SentinelLabs also linked the DEADWOOD (Detbosit) wiper to its operations [S4]. In 2022 the group used a software supply-chain compromise to deliver the Fantasy wiper (built largely on Apostle code) with the Sandals lateral-movement and execution tool [S6]. In 2023 it used Moneybird, a C++ ransomware [S7], and the MultiLayer, PartialWasher and BFG Agonizer wipers plus Sqlextractor, a database-extraction tool [S8][S9]. Its pattern is to steal data first, then wipe to cover tracks and make endpoints unusable [S8]. In the Unit 42 incident the actor tried and failed to bypass the endpoint security product [S9]. MITRE lists nine software entries for G1030 [S3].

campaigns.name: Shirbit insurance attack
campaigns.summary: Coverage of Check Point's research attributes ransomware on the Israeli insurer Shirbit in late 2020 to Agrius. 2021 reporting tied the attack to the group through unnamed industry sources.

campaigns.name: Apostle / DEADWOOD wiper-to-ransomware operations (SentinelLabs disclosure)
campaigns.summary: SentinelLabs reported Agrius wiper attacks on Israeli targets disguised as ransomware. Tools included the Apostle wiper, later made into working ransomware, the IPsec Helper backdoor and the DEADWOOD wiper. SentinelLabs assessed Iranian origin with medium confidence.

campaigns.name: Bar-Ilan University wiper attack
campaigns.summary: Press coverage of Check Point's research attributes wiper attacks on Israel's Bar-Ilan University in 2021 to Agrius.

campaigns.name: Fantasy wiper supply-chain attack (diamond industry)
campaigns.summary: Agrius abused an Israeli software developer's diamond-industry suite to deploy the Fantasy wiper and Sandals tool. Credential harvesting at a South African victim on 2022-02-20 preceded wiping on 2022-03-12. Victims were in Israel, South Africa and Hong Kong. ESET disclosed the campaign on 2022-12-07.

campaigns.name: Agonizing Serpens campaign against Israeli higher education and technology
campaigns.summary: From January to October 2023 the group stole PII and intellectual property, then deployed the MultiLayer, PartialWasher and BFG Agonizer wipers. Unit 42 reported the campaign in November 2023.

campaigns.name: Moneybird ransomware
campaigns.summary: Check Point incident responders found Moneybird, a new C++ ransomware, in an attack on an Israeli organization and attributed it to Agrius based on TTPs.

campaigns.name: Collaboration with Hezbollah cyber units
campaigns.summary: Microsoft detected collaboration between Pink Sandstorm and Hezbollah cyber units after the October 2023 war began.

campaigns.name: Israeli hospital hack-and-leak (Ziv Medical Center, per Israeli reporting)
campaigns.summary: Microsoft reports a Pink Sandstorm hack-and-leak against an Israeli hospital in late November 2023, apparently in retaliation for the al-Shifa siege. Israeli authorities reportedly attributed an attack on Ziv Medical Center to Iranian intelligence (naming Agrius) and Hezbollah's Lebanese Cedar unit. The data was leaked under the 'Malek Team' name.

diamond.adversary: Iranian operators, assessed by Microsoft as MOIS-linked [S1]. Israel reportedly attributed the group's 2023 hospital attack to Iranian intelligence working with Hezbollah [S10].
diamond.capability: ASPXSpy web shells, the IPsec Helper backdoor, and a run of wipers and fake ransomware: Apostle, DEADWOOD, Fantasy, Moneybird, MultiLayer, PartialWasher and BFG Agonizer. Also Sandals and Sqlextractor [S4][S6][S7][S8].
diamond.infrastructure: Compromised public-facing web servers used as entry points [S8]. A compromised software vendor's update path [S6]. Legitimate file-hosting platforms used to stage payloads [S7]. Microsoft reports infrastructure-level collaboration with Hezbollah cyber units but gives no indicators [S1].
diamond.victim: Israeli higher-education, technology, healthcare, insurance and diamond-trade organizations, plus supply-chain victims in South Africa and Hong Kong [S1][S6][S7][S8].
diamond.socioPolitical: Iran-Israel conflict. Destructive attacks are framed as criminal ransomware for deniability [S4][S7], and leaks retaliate for Israeli military actions in Gaza [S1].
diamond.technology: Unpatched internet-facing web applications, Windows/.NET environments, database servers and vendor software-update mechanisms [S6][S8].

gaps: Primary vendor reports could not be opened (SentinelLabs, ESET WeLiveSecurity, Unit 42, Check Point, CFR were unreachable by fetch). Their content here comes from search-result summaries and secondary coverage [S4][S6][S7][S8].

The web search budget ran out before searches for Microsoft's 2023 Iran report (AMERICIUM/MOIS), Check Point's Iran capabilities overview and any 2024-2026 Pink Sandstorm activity. No post-2023 campaigns are recorded here, including any activity during the 2025-2026 Israel-Iran hostilities.

Microsoft does not name the hospital in its report [S1]. The link to Ziv Medical Center rests on Israeli press reporting of government statements [S10]. Leaked-data volumes differ between outlets and are unverified.

The BlackShadow, Justice Blade, SharpBoys and FireAnt names appear in Microsoft's mapping [S2]. The sources here do not establish whether they are personas or separate vendor clusters, so no activity under those names is recorded here.
Microsoft's Hezbollah collaboration claim gives no technical detail (shared infrastructure, tools or division of labor) in the public report [S1].
Exact CVEs used for initial access are not given in the sources reviewed.
No US government (CISA, FBI, DOJ, Treasury) attribution of Agrius/Pink Sandstorm was located in this research pass.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: The operational environment is the Iran-Israel conflict. Key terrain includes internet-facing web servers, database servers holding PII and IP, and software vendors' update channels that reach downstream customers [S6][S8]. STEP 2: Initial access through known web-server vulnerabilities and ASPXSpy web shells means that patch latency on public-facing systems sets the window of exposure [S7][S8]. STEP 3: The doctrinal template is exploit a web server, drop a web shell, harvest credentials, move laterally, steal data, then deploy a wiper or fake ransomware, followed by leaks or ransom notes for influence effect [S4][S6][S8]. STEP 4: MLCOA is a destructive attack disguised as ransomware against Israeli or Israel-linked civilian institutions (education, health, tech), timed to retaliate for kinetic events [S1][S8]. MDCOA is a supply-chain wiper deployment through a trusted vendor that reaches multinational victims, including US or coalition partners sharing that vendor, possibly coordinated with Hezbollah cyber units [S1][S6]. Candidate indicators: new ASPX files or 'Certificate' text files on IIS servers [S7]; unexpected .NET or C++ binaries fetched from file-hosting sites [S7]; mass file deletion or boot-sector modification [S8]; bulk database extraction before destructive activity [S8].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: a ransomware event at a partner organization during an Israel-related crisis should be checked for wiper behavior and Iranian state links before it is treated as crime, because this actor deliberately disguises destruction as ransomware [S4][S7]. (2) Authorities: the attribution behind this record is vendor and Israeli government reporting, not US government reporting, so response actions relying on state attribution need validation through official channels [S1][S10]. (3) Mission assurance: inventory third-party software with auto-update paths and internet-facing IIS/web servers on DoD-adjacent networks. The Fantasy supply-chain case shows that victims can be reached through a vendor rather than targeted directly [S6]. Offline backups limit wiper impact. (4) Coordination: share indicators with Israeli and Gulf partners through existing channels. Track Hezbollah-linked cyber activity jointly with Iranian MOIS activity, given Microsoft's reporting that the two collaborate [S1].
